faq.a: Abdulaziz represents Arabic عَبْدُ الْعَزِيز, meaning servant of the Mighty.

faq.q: What is the origin of Abdulaziz?
faq.a: The name is Arabic and is a compound of عبد and a second element.
Yes. The underlying compound is عَبْدُ الْعَزِيز (ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz).

faq.q: What is the root of Abdulaziz?
faq.a: عبد is related to ع ب د; al-ʿAzīz is related to ع ز ز (ʿ-z-z).
Abdulaziz is a traditional Muslim personal name because it contains a compound invoking al-ʿAzīz, a divine epithet in Islamic tradition.
This record does not establish Abdulaziz as an explicitly named Qur'anic person; the compound's religious meaning is distinct from personal-name attestation in the text.

faq.q: What does Abdulaziz mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, the name means servant of the Mighty; the compound combines عبد with al-ʿAzīz.
The supplied “ab-du-la-ziz” is an approximate pronunciation; local pronunciations vary.

faq.q: Is Abdulaziz a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: The record classifies the name as masculine, consistent with traditional usage; regional frequency data is not supplied.
